requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as a managed service on node1
requirements.summary: Unit file inventory-worker.service sets ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker; systemctl show and ps confirm the MainPID process is executing that exact script, both immediately after setup and after a reboot.

Unit file created at /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service; systemctl is-active/is-enabled and systemctl show all target inventory-worker.service and report active/enabled both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service must run under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: id inventorysvc initially failed (no such user); useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin inventorysvc created uid 996, confirmed by id. Unit file sets User=inventorysvc, Group=inventorysvc, and the running process is directly observed executing as user inventorysvc via ps, both pre- and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service must be managed (enabled/started, persistent) via systemd
requirements.summary: systemctl daemon-reload, enable --now succeeded; is-active/is-enabled report active/enabled. Persistence directly demonstrated: pre-restart boot_id f1afbc7f... (matching after_prepare snapshot) captured with service active, systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged, connectivity lost during two timed-out polls, then a new boot_id 1241b2b2... observed (matching after_executor snapshot), and the service confirmed active/enabled with a new MainPID running as inventorysvc after the reboot — a complete baseline/disruption/recovery transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied: /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker runs as a systemd service named inventory-worker under a newly created dedicated inventorysvc system account, and it is enabled/active. The independent provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also fully executed and directly observed: pre-restart boot identity and healthy service state, a reboot acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed after_prepare/after_executor snapshots), and recovered service state running as inventorysvc. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found beyond a trivial, expected reboot log residue.
limitations: No evidence was captured of the worker script's actual runtime behavior/output beyond process presence (it is a simple sleep loop per its source), so functional correctness of the worker's business logic (if any beyond the loop) is not independently verifiable from this evidence.

Listening-socket and temp-file differences between after_prepare and after_executor are attributable to the reboot (new sshd/chronyd PIDs, new boot-id-named private tmp dirs) and were not independently interrogated beyond the collector's bounded snapshot.
Requirement service-runs-worker-binary cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-service-worker

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command traces to a clear purpose: useradd for the dedicated account, unit-file authoring plus daemon-reload/enable for the service, and the reboot cycle for the mandatory restart evidence protocol. No troubleshooting dead-ends, no failed/conflicting services (failed-services empty before and after), no package-health regression (dnf consistency unchanged), and hardening options (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome) were added rather than weakened. The reboot produced a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log (from the backgrounded systemctl reboot redirect) and new systemd-private temp dirs consistent with the new boot session — both are expected, low-risk byproducts of a legitimate reboot rather than abandoned or unsafe residue, so only a minor deduction is applied.
